recipe:garlic-butter-shrimp-noodles:step.en: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil.
Finely slice the chilli. Peel and finely grate the garlic and ginger. Mix together all the sauce ingredients in a small bowl and set aside.

Place a large wok or frying pan over a medium heat. Add the butter and a drizzle of olive oil. Once melted and foaming, add the garlic, ginger and chilli. Cook for 2-3 mins, stirring constantly, until softened and lightly caramelised.
Add the prawns to the pan and cook for 1 min on each side until just turning pink.
Cook the udon noodles following pack instructions, then drain.

Add the spinach to the pan with the prawns and stir until just wilted. Tip in the noodles and pour in the sauce. Toss everything together over a high heat for 1-2 mins until the noodles are coated and glossy. Taste and season with more salt or black vinegar, if needed.
Roughly chop the cashews and toast them in a dry frying pan for 2-3 mins until golden and fragrant. Then stir through the noodles.
Divide the noodles between two bowls and top with the toasted chopped cashews and scatter over the peanuts, sliced spring onion and a drizzle of chilli oil, if using.

recipe:garlic-butter-shrimp-noodles:ingr.pt: 2 colheres de sopa de Molho de Ostras
1 colher de sopa de Molho de Soja Escuro
1 colher de sopa de Molho de Soja Claro
1 colher de chá de Vinagre Negro Chinês

recipe:healthy-chocolate-spread:step:0.en: Heat the oven to 180°C fan/350°F and line a baking tray with baking parchment.

recipe:healthy-chocolate-spread:step:1.en: Lay the hazelnuts and sunflower seeds on the tray in a single layer and toast in the. oven for 8-10 mins. Check continuously as oven temperatures vary and nuts burn quickly. You want the nuts and seeds to be golden.

recipe:healthy-chocolate-spread:step:2.en: Put the chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of barely simmering water, making sure the bowl does not touch the water. Stir until melted.

recipe:healthy-chocolate-spread:step:3.en: When the nuts are ready, transfer to a food processor or high-powered blender and blitz continuously for 6-8 mins (scraping down the sides when necessary) until smooth – the mixture will resemble nut butter.

recipe:healthy-chocolate-spread:step:4.en: Add the melted chocolate and maple syrup and blitz once more to combine. Spread on toast, or transfer to a jar and use within 2 weeks.

recipe:healthy-chocolate-spread:ingredie.pt: 1 colher de sopa de Xarope de Ácer

recipe:pasta-primavera:step:0.en: To make the blitzed pea mixture, add the garlic, pistachios, parmesan, the peas, the juice of your lemon and the basil leaves (saving a few for garnish) into a blender along with 3 tbsp of olive oil, 3 tbsp of water and a pinch of salt. Blitz until smooth.

recipe:pasta-primavera:step:1.en: Put the pasta onto boil in plenty of salted water. While it cooks, prepare the asparagus by removing the tough bottoms and the tips (make sure to reserve the tips). Now shave the main part of the stalks into strips using a vegetable peeler and set aside.

recipe:pasta-primavera:step:2.en: Once the pasta is about 2 mins from being ready, add the asparagus and the rest of your peas in along with the asparagus tips you saved earlier.

recipe:pasta-primavera:step:3.en: Drain everything (reserving a mug of cooking water) and return to the pan, add in the blitzed pea mixture along with a big splash of cooking water and mix well until creamy and saucy. Taste and add salt and another squeeze of lemon, if you like.

recipe:pasta-primavera:step:4.en: Plate up and top with a little more grated cheese and a pinch of chilli flakes.

recipe:pasta-primavera:ingredient:11.pt: 0,5 colher de chá de Flocos de Malagueta

recipe:meatball-gnocchi-bake:step:0.en: Soak the fresh breadcrumbs in the cream and set aside.

recipe:meatball-gnocchi-bake:step:1.en: Peel and finely chop the onion and garlic. Fry in a pan on a medium-low heat with a drizzle of olive oil.

recipe:meatball-gnocchi-bake:step:2.en: While it is frying, slice up the stalks of the parsley and add to the pan, mixing everything together until the ingredients have softened. Take off the heat.

recipe:meatball-gnocchi-bake:step:3.en: In a separate bowl place your minced beef. De-case the sausages, pushing the meat out of the sausage into the bowl and discarding the skins.

recipe:meatball-gnocchi-bake:step:4.en: Add the fried onion, garlic and parsley into the mix. Add your soaked white breadcrumbs to the bowl. Begin to mix everything together.

recipe:meatball-gnocchi-bake:step:5.en: Once mixed, create small meatballs, placing on a chopping board or tray. Cover and leave to rest in the fridge for 20 minutes.

recipe:meatball-gnocchi-bake:step:6.en: After 20 mins, remove the meatballs from the fridge and begin to cook the meatballs in a large deep frying pan on a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Gently turn the meatballs, letting them gain shape as they cook.

recipe:meatball-gnocchi-bake:step:7.en: Once they have browned off, add 2 tins of tomatoes to allow the meatballs to cook through.

recipe:meatball-gnocchi-bake:step:8.en: Add the gnocchi to the meatball pan and mix everything together, making sure everything is covered in tomato sauce. Let simmer for 5 mins.

recipe:meatball-gnocchi-bake:step:9.en: Top with mozzarella and pop your pan under the grill until bubbling - this will take a couple of mins. Serve and enjoy.

recipe:spicy-mushroom-ragu-with-pasta:st.en: Finely chop the walnuts or pulse in a food processor until coarse. Do the same with the mushrooms, working in batches if needed.

Heat the oven to 225°C fan. Spread the mushrooms out in a single layer across two lined baking trays. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 15 mins, then scatter over the walnuts and return to the oven for 5–10 mins until everything is golden and toasty.

Peel and finely chop the onion, garlic, celery and carrot. Heat a splash of olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion, celery and carrot, season, and cook for 10–12 mins until soft and golden. Stir in the garlic and cook for 2 more mins until fragrant.

Add the tomato purée and harissa powder to the pan. Cook for 2–3 mins to deepen the flavour. Tip in the tinned tomatoes, then fill the empty tin with water and add that too. Crumble in the stock cube and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the roasted mushrooms and walnuts, along with ¼ of the tomato tin filled with water. Simmer for 15 mins, stirring occasionally, until thick and rich. Season to taste.
Cook the pasta in salted boiling water according to the packet instructions until al dente. Reserve a mug of cooking water, then drain.

Finely grate the parmesan. Tip the drained pasta into the sauce with a splash of the cooking water and the parmesan. Take off the heat and stir well to emulsify—the sauce should cling beautifully. Add more water if needed.
Divide between bowls and top with torn basil and extra parmesan, if you like.

recipe:supergreen-matcha-smoothie-bowl:s.en: Chuck the banana, mango, pineapple, spinach, matcha, protein powder, almond milk, skyr, honey and chia seeds into a blender. Blitz until completely smooth and creamy – you want it super thick, so use a tamper or stop and stir between blends if needed.
Scoop the smoothie into a bowl. Top with sliced kiwi, strawberries, a sprinkle of desiccated coconut and some granola, if using.

recipe:steak-tacos-chilli-pineapple-sals.en: Steak Tacos With Chilli Pineapple Salsa

Roughly chop 8 of the garlic cloves and lob them into a bowl. Finely cut the coriander and add half to the bowl with the garlic. Cover with 4 tbsp of oil and the juice and zest of a lime. Season the steaks with salt and pepper and drop into the marinade. Leave for 30 mins or up to overnight.

While the steaks are marinating, make the pineapple salsa. Cut the pineapple into a fine dice. Now toast the peanuts and sesame seeds in a dry pan. Add the pineapple, peanuts and sesame seeds to a bowl. Add the chilli oil and a good whack of lime juice.

Fish the steaks out of the marinade and preheat a heavy frying pan over a high heat. When smoking hot, add a shot of oil and get the steaks in. Cook for 2-3 mins a side until charred and caramelised. Don’t be afraid of burning some of the marinade. Let the steaks rest for 5 mins.
Whack the avocados into a blender with the sour cream, remaining garlic cloves, coriander, and a squeeze of lime juice. Season and blend until smooth. Finely dice up your shallots.

Heat up your tortillas in a dry pan or over an open flame. Cut the steak into 2cm chunks and toss through any resting juices. Load up the tacos with avocado crema, the steak, fresh cut jalapeños, diced shallots, and the pineapple chilli salsa.

recipe:halloumi-grains-green-tahini:step.en: Cut the courgettes into irregular 4cm pieces. Break the halloumi down its natural split, then cut into chunky pieces about the same size as the courgettes.
Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the halloumi and cook on all sides until golden – no need for oil. Remove from the pan.
Add the olive oil to the pan, then fry the courgettes on both sides until charred. Remove and season with salt and black pepper.

For the dressing, add the basil, tahini, juice of the lemons, ½ the jalapeños and all the water to a blender and blitz until smooth. Season with salt and black pepper, then taste and adjust if needed.
Mix the quinoa with the courgettes and season with salt and black pepper. Thinly slice the remaining jalapeño.

Box or plate up the courgette quinoa and top with the halloumi and sliced jalapeño. If eating later, store the dressing separately in an airtight container. If eating now, drizzle the dressing over the top. Everything will keep well in the fridge for 3 days.

recipe:potato-rosti-recipe:name.en: Potato Rosti Recipe With Brown Butter Fried Eggs & Sage

recipe:potato-rosti-recipe:step:0.en: Peel and coarsely grate the potatoes into a clean tea towel. Halve and thinly slice the onion. Put the butter into a small bowl and melt in the microwave.

recipe:potato-rosti-recipe:step:1.en: Gather the top of the tea towel together so the potato is completely encased, then hold it over the sink and squeeze as much water as possible from the potato.

recipe:potato-rosti-recipe:step:2.en: Tip the dry potato into a clean bowl. Add the sliced onion along with 2 tbsp of the melted butter, then season really well with salt and pepper. Mix well.

recipe:potato-rosti-recipe:step:3.en: Heat a pat of the butter in a medium frying pan (roughly 28cm) over a medium heat, then pile in all of the potato – you want the potato to be about 2 ½ cm thick. Gently press to make sure there is lots of contact with the bottom of the pan.

recipe:potato-rosti-recipe:step:4.en: Fry for 6-8 mins until the bottom is super golden and caramelised. Carefully flip the rosti out onto a plate, then add a pat of more butter and slide the rosti back into the pan. Continue to cook for another 6-7 mins or until the bottom is a deep caramel colour and is super crunchy.

recipe:potato-rosti-recipe:step:5.en: Once you’ve flipped the rosti and got it back into the pan, get another frying pan over a high heat. Pour in the melted butter and cook for 1-2 mins, gently whisking, until smelling nutty and has turned a light golden colour. Crack in the eggs, then baste them with some of the butter and cook for 1-2 mins until the white is cooked through and the yolk is still runny. Add the sage into the butter in the gaps between the eggs and cook for 1 min, then remove from the heat.

recipe:potato-rosti-recipe:step:6.en: Slide the rosti out onto a board and cut into quarters. Put each onto a plate then top with a fried egg and some of the sage. Cut the lemon in half and squeeze into the butter, then spoon over. Serve with hot sauce for splashing over and a green salad.

recipe:ginger-chicken-brothy-greens:step.en: Thinly slice the spring onions and finely grate the ginger and garlic. Add them to a freezer-safe container, then top with the watercress. Lay the chicken thighs on top and pour over the soy sauce, white pepper and chicken stock. Close and pop your container in the freezer.

When you're ready to cook, tip the frozen block into a large saucepan and place it over a medium heat. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 15-20 mins, or until the chicken is fully cooked through and tender.
Using two forks, shred the chicken into pieces directly in the pan.
Ladle the soup into bowls and finish with a drizzle of chilli oil, if using. Dig in!

recipe:ginger-chicken-brothy-greens:ingr.pt: 4 Coxas de Frango sem Osso e sem Pele
4 colheres de sopa de Molho de Soja
0,25 colher de chá de Pimenta Branca em Pó

recipe:thai-sausage-breakfast-sandwich:s.en: For the quick pickle, finely slice the shallot into rings (use your thumb to reveal the rings), then place them into a small bowl. Peel and finely slice the garlic, then slice the chilli and strip the leaves of coriander, setting aside for later, then chop up the stalks.
Put a third of the coriander stems into a bowl (reserve the rest for the patty), add all the remaining pickle ingredients and set aside.
Squeeze the sausage meat from the casings into a medium-sized bowl and add all the remaining patty ingredients. Mix well with clean hands or a fork. Divide into two balls and leave in the fridge.

For the Thai omelette, whisk the cornflower with some cold water in a small bowl (at a ratio of 2:1 water to cornflour). Add the eggs and fish sauce and whisk to combine. Bring a medium-sized pan to high heat and add a glug of oil. When the oil is hot add the egg mixture, leaving it for a few seconds to puff up. Then take the pan off heat and drag the egg mixture from the edges to the centre to create large wavy folds whilst tilting the pan to fill any gaps with raw egg. When the egg has mostly set and looks silky, turn the heat off and roughly fold it into 2 pieces roughly the size of the bun. Set the eggs aside on a plate.

Cook the Thai sausage patties in the same pan, add a splash of oil and set the heat to low heat. Flatten the sausage patties into circles around 3 cm-thick (no wider than the bun, though they will shrink slightly). Add the patties to the pan, add a lid and cook for 5 mins, this is the secret to juicy patties. Remove the lid and don’t be alarmed by the lack of colour on the patties, flip the patties, turn the heat to medium and cook for 2-3 mins without a lid or until nicely caramelised.

Remove the sausage patties to a plate to catch any excess juices. Place the pan back on medium heat, and add the buns to the pan, mayo-side down. Press down evenly with your hands and toast until lightly golden brown. Swirl the buns around the pan to soak up all the delicious juices.

To assemble, spread half of the kewpie mayo over the bottom bun, then top with a handful of coriander leaves, one sausage patty, egg, a spoonful of pickles, then the rest of the kewpie mayo on the toasted side of the top bun.
Enjoy sliced in half, with more pickles on the side.

recipe:smoky-tempeh-breakfast-bowl:step:.en: Rinse the quinoa under cold water, then cook in a pan of salted boiling water for 12–15 mins until fluffy. Drain and set aside.
Slice the tempeh and chuck it into a bowl with the smoked paprika, soy sauce, maple syrup, half the olive oil and a pinch of black pepper. Toss to coat, then spread out on one side of a baking tray.

Toss the cherry tomatoes with the rest of the olive oil and some salt and pepper. Add to the other side of the tray, then slide it into the oven for 15 mins until the tomatoes are soft and blistered and the tempeh is golden.
Finely chop most of the parsley, saving a few leaves for garnish. Stir the chopped parsley through the cooked quinoa.

Grate the garlic and squeeze the lime. Add both to a blender with the edamame and a pinch of salt and pepper. Blitz until smooth, adding a splash of water if needed to loosen it to a hummus-like consistency.

Spoon the quinoa into a bowl and top with the roasted tomatoes and crispy tempeh. Add a big dollop of the edamame guac and finish with the rest of the parsley. Serve with a wedge of lime on the side, if you like.

recipe:spicy-miso-dense-bean-salad:step:.en: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. Add the edamame beans and boil for 5 mins, then drain and rinse under cold water. Drain and rinse the cannellini beans.
Slice the romaine lettuce. Halve the cucumber lengthways, scoop out the seeds and slice. Finely slice the spring onions.
In a large bowl, whisk together the white miso, gochujang, maple syrup and rice vinegar until smooth.
Add the cannellini beans, edamame, quinoa, lettuce, cucumber and spring onions. Toss everything together and season with salt to taste.

Top with the toasted sesame seeds and torn coriander leaves before serving.If making ahead, box up and chill until needed. The salad will keep for up to 3 days in the fridge. Store the dressing separately to keep the salad fresh.

recipe:spicy-miso-dense-bean-salad:ingre.pt: 1 Saqueta de 250g de Quinoa para Micro-ondas

recipe:yoghurt-bowl-with-high-protein-gr.en: Combine the yoghurt in a bowl alongside your homemade high-protein granola.
Top with your choice of fresh fruit - we used kiwi, blueberries, and strawberries.

recipe:new-york-style-poppy-seed-bagels-.en: New York Style Poppy Seed Bagels & Lox

Tip the flour and yeast into a bowl with the sugar and fine salt. Blend the dry ingredients together before tipping in the warm water. Use your hand to bring the ingredients together into a shaggy dough. You want to incorporate all of the flour in the bowl, so keep mixing until there are no dry spots left!

Tip the dough out onto your countertop and knead for 8-10 mins until it is smooth, springy and has lots of strength. You can test this a few different ways, but my go-to is the window-pane test: using your thumb and forefinger on each hand, grab a corner of your dough and stretch it out as thin as you can. You should be able to see light passing through it (like a windowpane) before it tears. If it tears too easily, get back to kneading!

Once you’re happy with the gluten development, pop the dough into a bowl and cover. Allow to prove at room temperature for about an hour, or until doubled in size. Once proved, tip the dough back out onto your worktop and divide into 100-110g pieces. Flatten each piece into a long rectangle. Roll the dough up into a sausage, roughly 20-22cm long and about an inch thick.

To form the classic bagel shape, join the two ends of the sausage in the palm of your hand, wrapping the loop around the top of your hand. Roll the two ends together between your palm and the worktop, joining them together. Roll them until the join is roughly the same size as the rest of the bagel.

Line a couple of trays with parchment paper and set the bagels out on them to prove. Make sure you give them plenty of space to grow and cover them loosely with plastic wrap. You can either prove them at room temperature for an hour or so (until doubled in size) or you can do it overnight in the fridge. I prefer the overnight prove as you get a much nicer texture and flavour!
When your bagels are just about proved, preheat the oven to 220°C and set up a tray filled with the poppy seeds. Cut the paper between the bagels so each is sitting on a little square of parchment.

Fill a large pot with water (roughly 5 litres) and add the treacle and bicarbonate of soda. Whisk to combine and set over a high heat. Bring to a boil and then carefully lower in your proved bagels on the paper, peeling it off once they’re floating. Cook for about 30 seconds a side (flipping them over so both sides cook) before scooping them out with a slotted spoon or spider. Drop them straight into the poppy seed filled tray and flip them around a few times, completely coating them in the seeds. Repeat with the remaining bagels.
Put the poached bagels back onto a tray lined with parchment and slide into the oven for 20 mins until a deep golden brown. Whip them out and allow to cool on a rack for at least 15-20 mins.
Split the bagels in half and stuff with sliced smoked trout, cream cheese, sliced raw red onions and capers.

recipe:sticky-pomegranate-glazed-chicken.en: Sticky Pomegranate Glazed Chicken & Herby Quinoa
Stir the Lebanese 7-spice and 1 tablespoon of olive oil together in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper, then toss the chicken thighs through the marinade. Set aside to marinate.
Cook the quinoa following pack instructions. Once done, set aside to cool slightly.

Finely mince the parsley and coriander (stalks and all). Tip into a bowl with the quinoa and pomegranate seeds. Roughly crush the walnuts and add those in too. Stir through the olive oil, season with salt, and squeeze over the juice of the lemon. Give everything a good mix and adjust the seasoning to taste.
Set a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the chicken thighs and cook for 10–15 mins, turning halfway, until golden and cooked through.
Pour in the pomegranate molasses and honey. Take the pan off the heat and baste the chicken in the sticky glaze for a minute or two until coated and glossy.

Spoon the quinoa salad into Tupperware containers. Top with the glazed chicken and any juices from the pan. Serve with any leftover lemon wedges on the side. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

recipe:kimchi-baked-beans-with-sesame-fr.en: Kimchi Baked Beans With Sesame Fried Eggs

Start by finely dicing your bacon, finely chopping the onion and finely slicing the garlic. Heat your oil in a large pan and fry the bacon and onion for 8 mins, until the bacon is lightly golden. Add in the garlic and cook for 1 min before adding the tomato purée. Cook out for 1 min, until darkened in colour. Next add the brown sugar, smoked paprika, and soy sauce.

Drain your beans and add them to the pan along with the passata, kimchi, and a splash of water. Cook for 5 mins until reduced and thickened, adding another splash of water if drying out. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.

Heat 4 tbsp of oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Crack in your eggs and sprinkle with the sesame seeds. Cook until crisp around the edges and remove from the pan, draining on some kitchen roll.

Finely chop the spring onions. When the beans have reduced, pop some toast in the toaster or into a grill pan, cooking until golden. Serve the beans on toast topped with a sesame egg and garnished with spring onions.

recipe:nourishing-lemon-herb-chicken-sou.en: Finely chop the dill and parsley, including the stalks! Peel and cut the carrot into thin matchsticks (or very finely dice). Finely slice the celery and grate the garlic.

Add the dill, parsley, ditalini (any other small pasta shape will do!), carrot, garlic and celery to a freezer safe Tupperware along with the chicken stock and the zest of the lemon. Top with the chicken breast, seasoning it with salt and pepper, then pop into the freezer until ready to use.
When you're ready to cook, transfer the frozen contents of the Tupperware into a saucepan set over a medium heat. Cover with a lid, allow to melt. Then simmer the soup for 10 mins.
Flip the chicken and cook for another 5 mins, until the chicken is cooked through. Once cooked, remove the chicken from the pan and shred into bite-sized pieces and add back into the soup.
Season to taste with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Sprinkle over some parm and chilli flakes if you fancy too and dish up.

recipe:shredded-chicken-warming-spring-o.en: Shredded Chicken & Warming Spring Onion Brothy Rice
Cook the rice following packet instructions.

Trim and thinly slice the spring onions. Finely grate the ginger. Add both into a saucepan, with a drizzle of sesame oil. Set the pan over a medium heat and gently cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 mins until the onions have wilted.

Add the white pepper and pour the chicken stock in. Let it come to the boil then turn the heat down to low-medium, season with salt and gently drop the chicken thighs in. Leave for 10-15 mins until fully cooked.
Meanwhile, trim and chop the pak choi into 2-3cm chunks. Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems.
Once the chicken is cooked, use a slotted spoon to transfer it from the broth to a large bowl. Leave to cool for a couple of mins, then use two forks to shred it. Cover to keep warm.

Add the coriander stems and pak choi into the hot broth and cook for 2-4 mins, until wilted. Then use a slotted spoon to transfer the veg to the chicken bowl. Add the sesame oil and coriander leaves and toss to combine. Taste and season the broth with salt and white pepper, if needed.
To serve, share the rice between bowls and ladle the broth over. Top with the chicken mixture and a drizzle of chilli oil.

recipe:shredded-chicken-warming-spring-o.pt: 6 Coxas de Frango Sem Osso e Sem Pele

recipe:chipotle-mushroom-egg-breakfast-t.en: Heat the oven to 200°C. Slice the mushrooms into 1cm-thick slices. Put the chipotle into a large bowl with a generous drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and toss through the sliced mushrooms. Put the mushrooms onto a baking tray and roast for 15-20 mins until golden brown.
Meanwhile, put all the crema ingredients (minus the lime) into a blender and blitz until smooth. Zest half the lime in, then taste and season with salt, pepper and lime juice.

Crack the eggs into a bowl, season with salt and whisk together until smooth. Place a dry non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, toast the seeds (you know they’re ready once they start popping) and then transfer to a bowl.
Add a drizzle of oil to the now-empty frying pan, then pour the eggs in. Continuously stir until a fluffy scramble forms. Remove from the heat whilst the eggs are still slightly runny.
Heat the tortillas in a dry frying pan, then load them up with crema, chipotle mushrooms, scrambled eggs, toasted seeds, coriander and chilli flakes. Serve with any remaining lime, cut into wedges.

recipe:smacked-cucumber-dumpling-salad:s.en: For the dressing: stir all the creamy tahini dressing ingredients together into a bowl, adding 1 tbsp of cold water at a time until the dressing goes creamy. Taste and season with more sugar or soy sauce, if needed.
For the salad: add the rice vinegar, soy sauce and sesame oil into a bowl.

Trim the cucumber. Cut it into quarters, widthways. Using a rolling pin or something heavy, smack the cucumber until it splits. Chop into roughly 2cm large chunks. Trim and thinly slice the radishes and spring onion. Add the cucumber, spring onion whites and radishes into the dressing and toss together, let marinate for 5-10 mins.
Meanwhile, pan-fry the dumplings according to package directions.

Spoon the tahini dressing onto a sharing plate. Toss the dumplings into the cucumber salad and spoon over the creamy dressing. Sprinkle over the remaining spring onions and drizzle over the chilli oil.

recipe:miso-butter-salmon-rice:step:0.en: Rinse the sushi rice until the water runs clear, then cook with the measured water using your preferred method (rice cooker or saucepan). Set aside with the lid on to steam. Soft boil the eggs (cook them longer if you prefer).

recipe:miso-butter-salmon-rice:step:1.en: Season the salmon fillets with salt and leave to sit while you prep the rest.

recipe:miso-butter-salmon-rice:step:2.en: In a small bowl, mix the softened butter with the white miso until smooth and combined.

recipe:miso-butter-salmon-rice:step:3.en: Finely slice the cucumber and add to a bowl with the rice vinegar, sugar, soy sauce and the juice of half a lemon. Toss together and leave to lightly pickle. Then trim and thinly slice the spring onions and set aside for later.

recipe:miso-butter-salmon-rice:step:4.en: Pat the salmon dry with kitchen paper and spread the miso butter evenly over the top of each fillet. Place under a hot grill for 4–6 mins until golden and cooked through, with the butter bubbling.

recipe:miso-butter-salmon-rice:step:5.en: Meanwhile, set a saucepan filled with water over medium heat and bring to the boil. Once, boiling, reduce the heat and carefully drop in your eggs. After 5-6 minutes remove and place in a bowl of cold water. Once they're cool enough to handle peel the shell off.

recipe:miso-butter-salmon-rice:step:6.en: Fluff the rice and divide between bowls. Top each portion with a salmon fillet and any of the miso butter from the tray. Finish with the sliced spring onion and a pile of the pickled cucumber.

1 colher de sopa de Molho de Soja

recipe:maple-bacon-egg-cheese-bagels:ste.en: Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk together with the salt. Slice the bagels in half, spread the cream cheese onto the cut sides.

Place a frying pan over medium heat. Add the bacon rashers in and fry for 6-8 mins until crisp. Take it off the heat and drizzle over the maple syrup and toss to coat. Break the bacon into shards, then tip onto a plate to cool down.

Return the pan to a medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add a ladle full of the whisked egg and swirl it around so it covers the bottom of the pan. Sprinkle some maple bacon on top and place both bagel halves, cream cheese side down, onto the eggs.

Once the eggs are cooked, place a plate over the pan and flip everything out. Fold any overhanging egg in, and top one bagel half with 2 cheese slices. Drizzle over any maple bacon sauce and sandwich them together.
Wrap the bagels in foil, and let the cheese melt for a couple of minutes before tucking in.

If you're making these ahead of time, let them cool completely and then wrap and freeze. Unwrap and defrost the bagels in the microwave or overnight in the fridge, then reheat in a 180°C oven for 8-15 mins, until hot throughout.

recipe:egg-cheese-breakfast-quesadillas:.en: Crack the eggs into a large mixing bowl and whisk together with a good pinch of salt.

Melt the butter in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Once foaming, pour in the eggs. Using a rubber spatula, continuously move the eggs around from the edge into the centre until you have small curds forming. Remove from the heat and continue to cook the eggs in the residual heat of the pan until they are quite dry – further than you would normally take them for regular scrambled eggs.
Add the cream cheese to the pan and mix through. This will moisten the eggs and really help when reheating. Set aside and leave to cool slightly.

Now let’s build the quesadillas. Lay out the flour tortillas and sprinkle the grated mozzarella evenly over each one. Top with some of the egg mixture then fold the wrap in half. Pop them folded up into an airtight container, stacking them on top of each other (or wrap them up individually in clingfilm) and store in the fridge for up to 4 days.

If you’re adding any optional extras to the quesadillas (crispy cooked bacon, diced kimchi or thinly sliced spring onion), just pull the quesadillas open before cooking and add the additional ingredients.

When you’re ready to eat, place a non-stick pan over a medium heat. Once warm, add the quesadilla and cook for 2 mins on each side, until nicely browned and the cheese is melted. Cover in hot sauce and serve with a wedge of lime. Enjoy.

recipe:spicy-breakfast-burrito:step:0.en: Whisk the eggs in a large bowl with some salt and pepper.

recipe:spicy-breakfast-burrito:step:1.en: Add the chorizo into a hot pan and cook for 8 mins. Remove and set aside, leaving behind the stained chorizo oil.

recipe:spicy-breakfast-burrito:step:2.en: Turn the heat down to the lowest setting and pour in your eggs. Using a spatula cook for 3 - 5 mins on a very low heat stirring constantly until the eggs are just set.

recipe:spicy-breakfast-burrito:step:3.en: Finely chop the tomatoes, red onion and coriander. Mix this all in a bowl with some hot sauce and the juice and zest of a lime.

recipe:spicy-breakfast-burrito:step:4.en: Grate the cheese and scoop the meat out of the avocado, slice thinly.

recipe:spicy-breakfast-burrito:step:5.en: Grab your tortilla and add in ¼ of the eggs. Add a few tablespoons of salsa, chorizo then cheese and finally avocado. Roll tightly in a burrito fashion and then toast on a dry saucepan seam side down.

recipe:spicy-breakfast-burrito:step:6.en: Wrap in foil to keep warm and enjoy.

recipe:cherry-bakewell-overnight-oats:st.en: Chuck the oats into a bowl with the yoghurt, milk, vanilla extract, half the almond extract and the protein powder, if using. Mix well to combine, then set aside.
In a small bowl, stir together the almond butter, the remaining almond extract, two-thirds of the maple syrup and a pinch of salt. Set aside.

Tip the frozen cherries into a small saucepan with the rest of the maple syrup. Set over a low-medium heat and cook until the cherries have defrosted and are starting to release their juices. Roughly mash with a potato masher, leaving a few chunky bits.
Spoon the cherry mixture into the bottom of your containers. Top with the oats, then drizzle over the almond butter mixture. Finish with a scattering of toasted flaked almonds.
Cover and place in the fridge overnight.

recipe:bean-cheese-brekkie-quesadilla:st.en: Finely dice the onion and finely grate the garlic.

Heat a frying pan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the onion and cook for 6–7 mins until soft and translucent. Stir through the garlic and mixed herbs, then cook for about 30 seconds until the garlic smells mellow.
Add the beans – liquid and all – along with half the salsa. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 10–15 mins until it thickens slightly.
Use a masher to mash about half the beans in the pan. This helps the mix hold together. Season with salt and pepper, then let it cool slightly.

Lay 1 slice of cheese onto the tortillas, spoon the beans onto one half. Fold in half, stack the uncooked quesadillas on top of each other.
If making ahead, stack into a sandwich bag or box and freeze. 
If cooking straight away, toast the quesadillas in a dry frying pan over a medium heat until golden and the cheese is gooey.

If cooking from frozen, heat a drizzle of oil in a frying pan over a low-medium heat. Add the frozen quesadillas, cover with a lid, and cook gently until defrosted. Remove the lid, turn up the heat slightly and cook until crisp and golden.
Serve with hot sauce and remaining salsa.

recipe:chicken-cottage-cheese-meatballs-.en: Chicken & Cottage Cheese Meatballs with Butter Beans
Heat the grill to high. Peel and finely grate the garlic. Pick the parsley leaves and finely chop them.

Chuck half the garlic and one-third of the chopped parsley into a mixing bowl with the chicken mince and cottage cheese. Grate over the zest of half the lemon and finely grate in half the Parmesan. Season well with salt and black pepper.
Shape into golfball-sized meatballs with wet hands and place them onto a foil-lined baking tray.
Grill the meatballs for about 15 mins, until golden and cooked through.

Meanwhile, dump the butter beans (liquid and all) into a small frying pan and bring to a simmer. Fold through the spinach to wilt. Tip any juices from the chicken into the beans and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Grate over the remaining lemon zest and squeeze in the juice from a quarter of the lemon. Cut the rest into wedges for serving.

Spoon the beans into Tupperware containers and top with the meatballs. Sprinkle over the remaining chopped parsley, garlic, and chilli flakes then grate over the remaining Parmesan. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch - they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

recipe:peanut-butter-chicken-curry:step:.en: Chop the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Juice the lime, and add to a large bowl with all the remaining marinade ingredients, mixing to combine. Add the chicken pieces and toss, ensuring they are well coated in the marinade. Cover and chill for 1-2 hrs, or overnight for best results.

Once marinated, grill or air fry the chicken on the highest setting for 10-15 mins until charred in places. Don’t worry if the chicken hasn’t cooked through fully – it will be simmered in the curry later. Set aside.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion and chop the coriander. Set aside.

Heat the oil in a large pan over a medium heat and add the chopped onion. Cook for 5-6 mins until they start to brown slightly. Add the ginger and garlic pastes and cook for 2-3 mins until fragrant. Stir in the chopped tomatoes and tomato purée, then cook until the mixture thickens and the oil starts to separate from the sauce.

Add the ground coriander, garam masala, kasoori methi, chilli powder and 1 tsp salt to the tomato mixture. Cook for 2 mins. Lower the heat and stir in the peanut butter until fully incorporated. Pour in the cream, mixing well to create a smooth, creamy sauce. Let the curry simmer for 10 mins, adding a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Return the cooked chicken to the pan, stirring to coat it in the sauce. Simmer for 6-8 mins to ensure the chicken is heated through.
Top with chopped coriander and a drizzle of cream or melted butter, just before serving.

recipe:creamy-sun-dried-tomato-pasta-sal.en: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta according to the packet instructions until al dente. Drain, reserving a splash of the pasta water, and leave to cool slightly. Finely chop the sun-dried tomatoes and garlic.
While the pasta cooks, heat the sun-dried tomato oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and chopped sun-dried tomatoes, cooking gently for 1–2 mins until fragrant.
Pop the spinach into a colander or sieve and pour over two kettles of boiling water to wilt it. Squeeze out any excess moisture.

Stir the cottage cheese, pasta, wilted spinach, and most of the basil through the sun-dried tomato mix. Add a splash of the reserved pasta water if needed to loosen, and season well with salt and pepper.
Serve topped with Parmesan shavings and the remaining basil. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

recipe:spiced-aubergine-lentil-stew-humm.en: Spiced Aubergine & Lentil Stew Hummus Bowl

Slice the aubergine into thick rounds, about 2cm thick. Lay them onto a tray, brush with olive oil on both sides, and season with salt and pepper. Add the cherry tomatoes to the tray around the aubergines. Roast for 15 mins, then flip the aubergines. Roast for another 10-15 mins until softened and golden.
Finely slice the onion and chilli. Mince the garlic and ginger.

Cook the onion until softened, about 7 mins. Add the minced garlic, ginger, and half of the sliced chilli, then the tomato purée and spices and cook for 1 minute. Add the plum tomatoes and fill the tin ¾ full with water. Break up the plum tomatoes with the spatula and add plenty of salt. Let it simmer for 15 mins on medium high until thickened. Add the cooked lentils and stir to heat through for a few mins, then remove from the heat.
Add the roasted cherry tomatoes and aubergine and stir.

To serve, spread a thick layer of hummus in a shallow bowl and top with the stew. Finish with a good squeeze of lemon, a drizzle of olive oil and tahini. Garnish the sliced chilli, any fresh coriander and capers.

recipe:nduja-anchovy-spaghetti:step:0.en: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil.

recipe:nduja-anchovy-spaghetti:step:1.en: Meanwhile, finely slice the garlic. Finely chop most of the parsley, saving a few leaves to serve. Then add the spaghetti to the boiling water and cook for 2 mins less than pack instructions.

recipe:nduja-anchovy-spaghetti:step:2.en: Whilst the spaghetti cooks, place a large frying pan over a medium heat and add a big glug of olive oil. Add the ’nduja and let it melt for 2-3 mins, stirring so it turns glossy.

recipe:nduja-anchovy-spaghetti:step:3.en: Add the garlic and anchovies, then cook for 2-3 mins, stirring, until the anchovies have melted into the oil. Turn the heat down and zest the lemon straight into the pan.

recipe:nduja-anchovy-spaghetti:step:4.en: Use tongs to transfer the cooked spaghetti straight into the frying pan with a big splash of the pasta water. Toss everything together for 1-2 mins until the sauce clings to the spaghetti, adding more pasta water if it needs it.

recipe:nduja-anchovy-spaghetti:step:5.en: Squeeze in ½ the lemon juice and grate in most of the parmesan, saving a little to serve. Add the parsley then toss again, adding a little more pasta water if you need to. Taste and season with salt and plenty of black pepper.

recipe:nduja-anchovy-spaghetti:step:6.en: Divide between bowls and finish with another grind of black pepper and the remaining parmesan cheese grated over. Scatter with the remaining parsley leaves. Serve with the remaining lemon half, cut into wedges.

recipe:nduja-anchovy-spaghetti:ingredien.pt: 1 Lata de 30g de Anchovas em Azeite

recipe:emergency-gyoza-soup:step:0.en: Bring 500ml water to a boil over a medium heat. Boil your frozen gyoza in the water for 2 mins (1 min less than the stated cooking time).

recipe:emergency-gyoza-soup:step:1.en: Meanwhile, add the soy sauce, balsamic vinegar, crispy chilli oil to a mixing bowl, crumble in the stock cube and give it a mix.

recipe:emergency-gyoza-soup:step:2.en: Finely slice your spring onions. Crack the egg into a separate bowl and give it a whisk.

recipe:emergency-gyoza-soup:step:3.en: Strain out the cooked gyoza from the pot of water and set aside. Add the ingredients in the mixing bowl to the cooking water (this will form the base of your soup).

recipe:emergency-gyoza-soup:step:4.en: Reduce the heat to low and drizzle in the egg to form thin wispy strands of egg, stirring continuously as you go.

recipe:emergency-gyoza-soup:step:5.en: Add the gyoza back in. Divide between bowls and top with sliced spring onions and sesame seeds and drizzle with extra crispy chilli oil, if desired.

recipe:emergency-gyoza-soup:ingredient:2.pt: 1 colher de sopa de Molho de Soja

recipe:emergency-gyoza-soup:ingredient:3.pt: 1 colher de sopa de Vinagre Balsâmico

recipe:emergency-gyoza-soup:ingredient:4.pt: 1 colher de chá de Óleo de Malagueta Crocante

recipe:emergency-gyoza-soup:ingredient:7.pt: 1 colher de chá de Sementes de Sésamo

recipe:emergency-gyoza-soup:ingredient:8.en: Crispy Chilli Oil (to taste, to serve, optional)
recipe:emergency-gyoza-soup:ingredient:8.pt: Óleo de Malagueta Crocante (a gosto, para servir, opcional)

recipe:miso-maple-chicken-with-rice-meal.en: Butterfly the chicken breasts and season both sides with salt and pepper. Crush the garlic cloves, discarding the skins.
Stir the maple syrup, soy sauce, miso and water together in a small bowl. Set aside.

Thinly slice the cucumber. Defrost the edamame. Fill a kettle and bring to the boil. Add the spinach to a colander and pour over the boiling water until wilted. Let it cool slightly, then squeeze out any excess water.
Tip the sliced cucumber into a bowl, season with salt and set aside.
Place a frying pan over a medium heat and add the olive oil. Pat the chicken dry, then place into the pan. Cook for 8–10 mins, flipping halfway, until golden on both sides.
Add the garlic and pour in the miso-maple mixture. Let it bubble away, basting the chicken as it cooks, until the sauce thickens into a glossy glaze and the chicken is cooked through.
Reheat the rice. Stir the edamame, spinach, rice vinegar and sesame seeds through the cucumber to make the salad.

Share the rice between Tupperware containers and top with the glazed chicken and crunchy salad. Spoon over any leftover glaze from the pan. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch - they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

recipe:miso-maple-chicken-with-rice-meal.pt: 3 colheres de sopa de Xarope de Ácer
0,5 colher de sopa de Molho de Soja
1 colher de sopa de Miso Branco
1 colher de sopa de Sementes de Sésamo Tostadas

recipe:zoe-granola:step:1.en: In a large bowl, mix together all the dry ingredients (everything except the coconut oil, honey and almond butter) along with a pinch of salt.

recipe:zoe-granola:step:2.en: In a separate jug or bowl, mix together the coconut oil, honey and almond butter until combined.

recipe:zoe-granola:step:3.en: Stir the wet ingredients through the dry mixture until everything is coated.

recipe:zoe-granola:step:4.en: Spread the granola mix out onto a lined tray, pressing it into a single flat layer.

recipe:zoe-granola:step:5.en: Bake for 25 mins, checking halfway and turning if necessary to ensure it browns evenly.

recipe:zoe-granola:step:6.en: Rest for 10 mins and do not touch the granola at all if you want large chunks

recipe:zoe-granola:step:7.en: Once the granola has cooled completely, it should break off into nice chunky pieces. Enjoy immediately or store in an airtight jar for up to a few weeks.

recipe:zoe-granola:ingredient:5.pt: 2 c. sopa de Sementes de Chia

recipe:zoe-granola:ingredient:7.pt: 1 c. sopa de Casca de Psyllium

recipe:zoe-granola:ingredient:8.pt: 2 c. chá de Canela em Pó

recipe:zoe-granola:ingredient:11.pt: 1 c. sopa de Manteiga de Amêndoa

recipe:sticky-mango-paneer-kebabs:step:0.en: Soak your wooden skewers in a tray filled with water. Cut your paneer into 3cm cubes and pop them in a large bowl.

recipe:sticky-mango-paneer-kebabs:step:1.en: For the paneer marinade, roughly chop the ginger and garlic then add to a food processor with the ground cumin, chilli powder and turmeric. Add the tomato purée, vegetable oil, ⅔ of the mango chutney and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Blend until you have a smooth paste. Pour the mixture over the paneer chunks and toss to coat. Leave to marinate for at least 30 mins, or pop in the fridge overnight if you have the time.

recipe:sticky-mango-paneer-kebabs:step:2.en: Meanwhile, thinly slice the red onion. Heat a little vegetable oil in a frying pan set over a medium heat. Add ½ the onions and cook them for 15 mins until they are totally soft and starting to caramelise. Add your curry powder and cook out for 2 mins until fragrant. Turn off the heat and leave the onions to cool a little.

recipe:sticky-mango-paneer-kebabs:step:3.en: Add the remaining onion to a bowl and squeeze over the lime juice. Sprinkle in a good pinch of salt, then scrunch up with your onions with your hands to encourage them to pickle. Set aside.

recipe:sticky-mango-paneer-kebabs:step:4.en: Spoon your caramelised onions into your food processor. Add the yoghurt and remaining mango chutney, then blitz until totally smooth. Set aside.

recipe:sticky-mango-paneer-kebabs:step:5.en: Heat your grill, BBQ or top broiler to a medium-high heat.

recipe:sticky-mango-paneer-kebabs:step:6.en: Skewer your paneer pieces onto your wooden skewers. If grilling/broiling, arrange your skewers on a baking tray and slide under the grill to cook for 6 mins on each side, turning until they're evenly cooked and starting to char a little around the edges. If barbecuing, place them on the grills and cook the paneer in the same way.

recipe:sticky-mango-paneer-kebabs:step:7.en: Heat your naans up in the oven following packet instructions. Roughly chop your coriander and slice your chillies.

recipe:sticky-mango-paneer-kebabs:step:8.en: To serve, spread a little yoghurt on the base of the naan, then push your paneer off your skewers on top. Finish with the pickled onions, chillies and fresh coriander.

recipe:cheesy-chorizo-brekkie-burritos:s.en: Start by cutting the potatoes into matchsticks and pop them into a bowl of ice-cold water. Set aside while you prep everything else. Drain and change the water twice to get rid of the starch.
Meanwhile, set a frying pan over a medium heat and add the chorizo. Fry for 8–10 mins until they are nicely caramelised and the oil’s released. Scoop out and set aside.
Pop the spinach into a colander and pour over a kettle of boiling water. Once wilted and cool enough to handle, squeeze out the excess water.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Pat the potatoes dry with kitchen paper and add them to the pan. Season with salt, pepper and the oregano. Cook until golden and tender – you’ll need to do this in batches to avoid overcrowding. Add the remaining oil in thirds as you go.

Crack the eggs into a bowl, season with salt and pepper, then whisk. Melt the butter in a large non-stick pan over a low heat. Pour in the eggs and gently stir until halfway cooked. Dollop in the soft cheese and fold gently with a spatula until creamy and just set – don’t overdo it. They'll keep cooking as you assemble.

Now you can assemble. Lay out the tortilla wraps on a chopping board. Start with a layer of crispy potatoes, then grated cheddar, spinach, scrambled eggs and finally chorizo. Fold in the sides, then roll up tightly into burritos.

To seal, heat a dry frying pan over a medium heat. Pop the burritos in seam-side down and cook for 1–2 mins until sealed. Alternatively, chuck them in the air fryer at 200°C for 5 mins. Once ready, wrap each burrito in a layer of baking paper followed by foil. Stash in the freezer for later.To reheat: Remove the foil, wrap the burrito in damp kitchen paper and microwave for 2 mins. Finish in the air fryer for 7–8 mins at 180°C (or in the oven for 10 mins at 160°C) until piping hot throughout.

recipe:tropical-sunshine-smoothie-bowl:s.en: Chuck the mango, pineapple, banana, milk, yoghurt, juice of the lime, turmeric, ginger and protein powder into a blender.

Start blending on a low speed. Use a tamper to push the mixture down – it’ll be thick, but that’s what we’re after. Only add more liquid if you really need to. Splash in an extra 10ml of milk at a time if it won’t budge.
Scoop into a bowl and top with whatever you fancy – banana slices, coconut flakes, granola, seeds or a drizzle of almond butter.

recipe:tropical-sunshine-smoothie-bowl:i.pt: 0,25 c. chá de Cúrcuma em Pó

recipe:spicy-salmon-bowl-with-sesame-ric.en: Spicy Salmon Bowl with Sesame Rice & Soy Butter Spinach

Wash the sushi rice until the water runs clear. Add the rinsed rice to a saucepan along with the water. Set the pan over a high heat and let the water come to the boil then cover with a lid, turn the heat down to low and leave to cook for 12 mins. Then turn the heat off and leave it covered, undisturbed for another 10 mins.

For the sauce, grate the garlic into a large bowl then add the remaining sauce ingredients and whisk until incorporated. Dice the salmon fillets into large cubes (about 3 per fillet) and add them to the sauce. Toss well to cover then transfer to a container and leave to marinate in the fridge.

Now let’s make the rice seasoning. In a small bowl, whisk together the salt, sugar and vinegar and set aside. In a blender, blitz the nori into small pieces or cut into small pieces. Once the rice is cooked, stir through the seasoning liquid, nori and sesame seeds.

For the spinach, thinly slice the garlic. Melt the butter in a medium saucepan set over a medium heat then add the sliced garlic and cook for about 3 mins until softened and fragrant. Add the spinach and gently wilt before seasoning with the soy sauce and a squeeze of lemon.
When you want to eat, pop the salmon in the air fryer and pour over the sauce. Cook at 240°C for 3-4 mins. Heat the rice in the microwave until piping hot, if needed. Thinly slice the spring onions.
To serve, spoon the rice into a bowl, top with the salmon, spooning over the sauce. Finish with the buttery spinach, spring onions and some extra nori, if you like.

recipe:thai-red-chicken-meatballs-with-p.en: Thai Red Chicken Meatballs with Peanut Sauce
Add a shot of oil to a small frying pan, then add the curry paste and fry for 3 mins. Set aside.

Finely chop the coriander stalks and transfer to a large bowl. Add the chicken mince and half of the fish sauce, then grate in the zest of 1/2 the lime. Add the fried curry paste, eggs, breadcrumbs and seasoning. Mix together really well until it becomes sticky. Form into 12 balls with wet hands, around 60g-70g each.
Heat a shot of oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and fry the meatballs for 10-15 mins until golden all over and cooked through.

For the sauce, get the coconut milk into a saucepan with the peanut butter and the remaining fish sauce. Melt and bring to a simmer, then season with salt and the juice of the remaining lime. Add the sugar, if necessary, to balance the flavour.
Trim and halve the green beans, finely chop the spring onions and pick the coriander leaves.
Cook the rice following pack instructions, then add the green beans 5 mins before the end of cooking time.

If batch cooking for the week, serve up a third of this meal for dinner then store the rest in containers (keep the meatballs, rice/beans, peanut sauce and spring onions separate). Use the leftovers to make our Thai Red Meatball Curry and Thai Red Fried Meatball Fried Rice with Crispy Egg.
Serve the rice and meatballs drizzled with peanut sauce. Top with spring onions and coriander, with a lime wedge on the side.

recipe:thai-red-chicken-meatballs-with-p.pt: 3 c. sopa de Pasta de Caril Vermelho Tailandês
3 c. sopa de Molho de Peixe
6 c. sopa de Manteiga de Amendoim

recipe:warming-bean-and-veg-soup:step:0.en: Soak your porcini mushrooms in around 100ml boiling water or until they are just covered.

recipe:warming-bean-and-veg-soup:step:1.en: Prep time. Chop your onions, celery, courgette and carrots into chunks and finely chop your herbs and garlic. Zest and juice your lemon.

recipe:warming-bean-and-veg-soup:step:2.en: Add your onions and carrots into a pan to cook first with some olive oil. Once those have softened slightly, add your celery and your courgette. After a couple of mins also add your garlic, chopped rosemary, oregano and chilli flakes

recipe:warming-bean-and-veg-soup:step:3.en: While that is cooking, drain your porcini mushrooms making sure to reserve the water. Chop then add into the pan along with your lemon zest.

recipe:warming-bean-and-veg-soup:step:4.en: Add the reserved mushroom stock to the pan along with your veg bouillon then add in your cannellini beans and water straight from the tin.

recipe:warming-bean-and-veg-soup:step:5.en: Roughly chop your tomatoes and add them in. Give everything a good mix.

recipe:warming-bean-and-veg-soup:step:6.en: Once all your veg has softened, add the remaining boiling water to your pan and simmer for 10 minutes.

recipe:warming-bean-and-veg-soup:step:7.en: Chop your chard and basil and add to the pan after 5 minutes. Let it wilt then finally add in the juice of your lemon and a good grinding of black pepper. Season to taste and serve. I like to eat mine with some toasted crusty bread. Enjoy!

recipe:warming-bean-and-veg-soup:ingredi.pt: 1 c. chá de Flocos de Malagueta
2 c. chá de Bouillon de Legumes em Pó

recipe:parmesan-fried-egg:name.en: Parmesan Fried Egg With Jalapeño Salsa

recipe:parmesan-fried-egg:step:0.en: Make the salsa first by finely dicing the shallot and jalapeño before combining them in a small bowl. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt and leave for 5 mins, before stirring in the lime juice, olive oil and finely chopped coriander.

recipe:parmesan-fried-egg:step:1.en: Coarsely grate the mature cheddar and finely grate the Parmesan. When you’re ready to eat, arrange the cheddar in a fried-egg-sized pile in a well-seasoned cast-iron or other non-stick pan and set it over a medium heat. Scatter the Parmesan over the top. Make an indent in the middle as a landing spot.

recipe:parmesan-fried-egg:step:2.en: Crack the egg into the target area before the cheese is fully melted, then fry for 2 ½ mins (or a tiny bit longer) until the cheese is golden and crisping. Remove from the heat before anything burns. If the egg white is not quite set, leave in the hot pan for 30–60 seconds more.

recipe:parmesan-fried-egg:step:3.en: Once off the heat, allow the cheese to cool and harden for 30-60 seconds more, warming the tortilla in a dry pan over a medium-high heat while you wait.

recipe:parmesan-fried-egg:step:4.en: Use a fish slice or spatula to carefully prize the egg and its crispy cheesy skirt from the pan, and transfer onto the warm tortilla.

recipe:parmesan-fried-egg:step:5.en: Spoon salsa liberally all over, fold in half and eat immediately. You’ll have some salsa leftover. Make another?

recipe:crispy-beef-dan-dan-noodles:step:.en: Start with the prep for your mince. Grate your ginger and slice the spring onions, set aside the green parts for garnish later.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the mince for 8 minutes, until the water has evaporated and the fat starts to render and sizzle.

Add the ginger and white parts of the sliced spring onion. Sauté for a couple of minutes until fragrant. Pour in the Shaoxing wine and cook for 2 mins, until the alcohol is cooked off. Then season with the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce and sugar. Keep on low heat so it stays warm.
Grate your garlic into a small bowl and add the remaining sauce ingredients, mixing everything together until smooth.
Boil the noodles according to packet instructions and add the choy sum for the final 45 seconds of cooking.

Toss the noodles with the sauce, loosening with a splash of noodle cooking water if needed. Plate with the choy sum and cooked mince, then finish with the green sliced spring onions, crushed peanuts and extra crispy chili oil, if you fancy.

recipe:crispy-beef-dan-dan-noodles:ingre.pt: 2 Ninhos de Massa de Trigo Fresca

recipe:blueberry-almond-smoothie:step:0.en: Chuck the blueberries, blackberries, banana, milk, protein powder, almond butter and chia seeds into a blender.

recipe:blueberry-almond-smoothie:step:1.en: Blend until smooth. If it’s looking a bit too thick, loosen with a splash of cold water.

recipe:blueberry-almond-smoothie:step:2.en: Pour into a glass and sip away.

recipe:garlicky-mustard-chicken-zingy-br.en: Garlicky Mustard Chicken & Zingy Broth With Rice
Add the chicken thighs and mustard to a bowl. Grate over the garlic and drizzle over some oil. Season generously with salt and pepper and give it a good mix. Set aside.
Reserve a few dill and parsley leaves for garnish and finely chop the rest, stalks included.
Heat a frying pan with a drizzle of oil over a medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken and cook on both sides until slightly charred and cooked through.
Reheat the cooked rice and stir through the herbs.

Heat the stock in a saucepan over a medium heat. Whisk the egg yolks in a small bowl with the juice of half your lemons then pour the egg mixture into the hot stock. Whisk vigorously until it starts to thicken slightly. Season with salt, pepper and more lemon juice to taste (you want it quite tart).
Share the rice between four bowls and ladle over the broth. Top with the chicken and reserved herbs. Serve with any remaining wedges of lemon.

recipe:garlicky-mustard-chicken-zingy-br.pt: 8 Coxas de Frango sem Osso e sem Pele
2 colheres de sopa de Mostarda de Grão

recipe:pink-power-smoothie:step:0.en: Add the strawberries, 50g of the raspberries, cherries, banana, almond milk, yoghurt and protein powder to a blender. Grate in the zest of the lime and then squeeze in the juice.

recipe:pink-power-smoothie:step:1.en: Blitz until smooth. Pour into a glass.

recipe:pink-power-smoothie:step:2.en: Crush the remaining 25g frozen raspberries with the back of a spoon, then spoon over the top. Serve straight away – cold, creamy and berry-packed.

recipe:pink-power-smoothie:ingredient:6.pt: 30g de Proteína em Pó de Baunilha

recipe:curried-coconut-chicken-rice:step.en: Put the chicken into a bowl. Grate the garlic on top, then stir half the oyster sauce through. Season with salt and pepper, then set aside to marinate. Pick the coriander and thinly chop the stalks. Set aside.

Place a saucepan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add a splash of coconut milk and cook for a couple of seconds. Stir through the coriander stalks, curry paste and remaining oyster sauce until fragrant. Add the water and remaining coconut milk, bring to the boil, then turn the heat down and simmer for 10-15 mins.

Meanwhile, place a frying pan with a drizzle of oil over a medium-high heat. Once hot, cook the marinated chicken on both sides, until slightly charred and cooked through. Taste and season the broth with lime juice, salt, sugar and pepper.
Divide the rice between bowls, ladle the soup on top and finish with sliced chicken. Drizzle over the chilli oil and scatter with your crispy onions. Finish with the coriander leaves.

recipe:caramelised-soy-chicken-in-garlic.en: Caramelised Soy Chicken in Garlic Ginger Broth with Rice

Bash the ginger and garlic, then transfer to a saucepan with the stock and place over a medium heat. Trim the spring onions, then thinly slice the green parts and halve the whites lengthways. Add the spring onion whites to the stock. Let the stock simmer away until hot while you make the rest of the recipe.
Put the chicken thighs into a bowl with the kecap manis, then season with salt and white pepper. Set aside to marinate.

Add the neutral oil to a frying pan with the spring onion greens and place over a high heat. Once the spring onions have wilted, tip them into a bowl. Stir through the sesame oil and toasted sesame seeds. Set aside.

Return the frying pan to a medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 7-8 mins until golden brown, caramelised and charring in spots. Pour water into the leftover marinade and pour over the chicken. Cook until reduced to a thick sauce.
Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice the cucumber and season with salt before serving. Reheat the cooked rice.
Share the rice between bowls. Ladle over the stock and top with the sliced chicken and cucumber. Drizzle with sambal/chilli sauce and the sesame spring onion oil.

recipe:caramelised-soy-chicken-in-garlic.pt: 8 Coxas de Frango Sem Osso e Sem Pele

recipe:batch-beef-chilli-con-carne:step:.en: Finely dice the onion and red peppers. Crush the garlic.
Add a drizzle of olive oil into a large lidded saucepan on medium heat. Once hot, fry the mince in batches, making sure it doesn’t stew. Once browned, remove from the pan and set aside.
Add another glug of oil into the pan. Then, add the onion and pepper. Stir-fry over until softened, 7 mins, then add the garlic and fry until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato purée, chilli powder, paprika and ground cumin. Cook for 2 mins stirring all the time.

Add the tinned tomatoes and drained kidney beans. Mix well, then return the mince to the pan and pour in the beef stock. The mince should all be covered. If not, add a splash of water. Season with salt and pepper. At this point, taste the chilli – if you want more spice, add a wee bit more chilli powder.

Simmer the chilli until thickened to your liking, or bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer, place a lid on and leave to cook gently for up to 1 hr 30 mins, depending on how much time you have. Simmering for a longer time will mean a thicker, richer end result, but it’s still delicious eaten straight away if you don’t have the time or are too hungry.
Stir the sweetcorn through until defrosted before serving. Optional: if batch cooking for the week, transfer to Tupperware containers.

recipe:green-tofu-udon:step:0.en: Start by making the crispy topping. Peel and slice the garlic, finely slice the chilli and peel and dice the shallot. Add to a small saucepan and cover generously with vegetable oil so the aromatics are fully submerged. Place the pan over a medium-high heat and cook for around 5-7 mins until browned and crispy.

recipe:green-tofu-udon:step:1.en: Use a slotted spoon to scoop out the crispy aromatics and add to a bowl. Season with the sugar and MSG, if using, and set aside. (Save the oil in the fridge for other uses, such as frying eggs.)

recipe:green-tofu-udon:step:2.en: Place a large pan of salted water over a high heat and bring to the boil. Once boiling, add the eggs and cook for 7 mins. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the eggs to a bowl. Rinse under cold water until cool enough to handle, then peel and set aside.

recipe:green-tofu-udon:step:3.en: While the eggs are boiling, start on the green sauce. Peel the garlic and pull the cavolo nero leaves away from the stems. Add the cavolo nero leaves, spinach, garlic and coriander to the boiling water used for the eggs and cook for 3 mins. Use tongs to transfer the greens to a sieve, then rinse with cold water until cool enough to handle.

recipe:green-tofu-udon:step:4.en: Squeeze out any excess moisture from the blanched greens, then add them to a blender along with the remaining sauce ingredients. Blitz until smooth, adding a splash of water to loosen a little, then tip the sauce into a large mixing bowl.

recipe:green-tofu-udon:step:5.en: Drop the udon into the boiling water and cook following packet instructions (about 2 mins for fresh or frozen udon). Use tongs to transfer the noodles to the mixing bowl of sauce then toss to coat.

recipe:green-tofu-udon:step:6.en: To serve, divide the noodles between bowls, scraping out all the sauce into the bowls. Top generously with the crispy garlic topping and finish with the halved boiled eggs.

recipe:chickpea-tahini-harissa-smoosh:st.en: Dice the peppers into small cubes and finely chop the parsley.
Combine all of the ingredients in a bowl (juicing in the lemon) and season with a generous amount of salt and pepper.
'Smoosh’ it over toast, pitta bread, a bagel or whatever you fancy. Sprinkle over some sesame seeds and any remaining parsley and enjoy.

recipe:ultimate-cauliflower-cheese:step:.en: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Cut the cauliflower into large florets, then cut the stem into 2cm pieces. Tip onto a baking tray along with any nice, young leaves from the cauliflower. Drizzle with a little oil, season well with salt and pepper and put into the oven for 25 mins until beginning to char at the edges.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan over a medium-high heat. Once foaming, tip in the flour and cook, stirring constantly, for 4-5 mins until the colour has noticeably darkened and it is smelling toasty. Lower the heat to medium. Measure the milk and cream into a large jug, then pour in a little bit of it and whisk furiously. Keep repeating this process until you have a luscious, smooth sauce.

Coarsely grate the cheddar and gruyère and scatter ¾ of it into the sauce, spoon in the mustard and finely grate in the nutmeg. Stir together over a medium heat until the cheese has melted into the sauce. Season with salt and pepper.

Once the cauliflower has roasted, tip it into a high-sided baking dish where the florets sit relatively snugly in an even layer. Pour the sauce over the top, then scatter with the remaining cheese. At this stage, you could cover and chill for up to 24 hours before finishing.
Turn or heat the oven to 200°C fan. Pop the cauli cheese in the oven (we like to put it on a flat baking sheet to catch any drips) and bake for 20-25 mins or until golden and bubbling.
Finely chop the chives and scatter over for a final allium punch.

recipe:green-goddess-chopped-salad:step:.en: Slice the cucumber in half lengthways and use a spoon to remove the fleshy center. Place the cucumber halves, lettuce, celery sticks, spring onions and sugar snaps on a board. Cut the cheeks from the apple and add to the board. Chop until all around the same size. Tip into a bowl and add the brown rice.
To make the dressing, halve and de-stone the avocado and add the flesh to a blender along with the green chilli, herb leaves and lemon juice. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Tip the dressing over the salad and toss well.
If you want to top with halloumi, cut the halloumi into 2cm cubes and pan fry in a dry pan over a high heat until golden on all sides. Tip on top of the salad and scatter with toasted sesame seeds.

recipe:full-vegan-breakfast:step:0.en: Start with the potatoes. Preheat the oven to 190°C. Cut the potatoes into quarters or halves if they are very small, making sure they are all a similar size. Place them into a baking dish with the tomatoes. Ideally the baking dish is not too big, so that everything fits snuggly in it, without too much empty space.

recipe:full-vegan-breakfast:step:1.en: Mix the gochujang with 1 tsp of sesame oil, 1 tbsp of olive oil, ¼ tsp salt, ¼ tsp maple syrup and plenty of black pepper. Pour this over the potatoes and tomatoes and mix well to make sure everything is well covered.

recipe:full-vegan-breakfast:step:2.en: Bake for 30-35 mins, tossing once or twice, until the potatoes are starting to crisp up on the edges and the tomatoes have yielded most of their juice.

recipe:full-vegan-breakfast:step:3.en: Next, marinate the tofu. Slice the block into thin slices, about 3 cm thick. Make the marinade in the dish or container that the tofu will fit in. Mix 2 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tsp maple syrup, ½ tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp tomato paste and 1 tbsp of olive oil. Pour this over the tofu and make sure all of the slices are covered. Set aside for now.

recipe:full-vegan-breakfast:step:4.en: To make the mushrooms, roughly chop any large ones into bite-sized pieces and place in a baking dish. Mince the garlic and add this to the mushrooms with plenty of salt and pepper and a good drizzle of olive oil. Use plenty of olive oil, ideally there will be a little extra at the bottom of the dish, this will help get them extra juicy. Roast for about 20 mins, until caramelised.

recipe:full-vegan-breakfast:step:5.en: Now, lay the tofu onto a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Make sure they are not overlapping. Bake for 8 mins, flip, brush with the extra marinade and bake for another 8-10 mins until it’s starting to crisp up on the edges.

recipe:full-vegan-breakfast:step:6.en: To air fry, cook them at 200°C for 10 mins, flipping them and brushing the marinade over halfway through.

recipe:full-vegan-breakfast:step:7.en: When they come out of the oven, brush them again with the remaining marinade. They should have a firm bite and be slightly crispy on the edges but not hard and crunchy.

recipe:full-vegan-breakfast:step:8.en: To heat the beans, decant them into a small baking dish and add 1 tsp of soy sauce and 1 tsp of smoked paprika and mix. If using, sprinkle over the vegan grated cheese, then bake for about 10 mins on the lower shelf, until bubbling.

recipe:full-vegan-breakfast:step:9.en: While everything is in the oven, slice your avocado and season with salt and pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. Toast and butter your bread with vegan butter. Finely chop the chives.

recipe:full-vegan-breakfast:step:10.en: To serve, dish out everything onto two plates or onto one big platter. Scatter over the chives and tuck in.

recipe:chicken-pesto-sun-dried-tomato-hi.en: Chicken, Pesto & Sun-Dried Tomato High Protein Smash
Shred the cooked chicken and add to a large bowl with the cottage cheese and pesto. Mix until the chicken is well coated.

Finely chop the sun-dried tomatoes and spinach, quarter the cherry tomatoes, tear the basil and finely slice the spring onion. Fold everything through the chicken mixture, then season with salt and black pepper and mix until evenly combined and thick enough to scoop.
To serve, toast the sourdough and dollop the smash mix generously onto each slice. Pop any leftovers in the fridge, it will keep for up to 3 days.

recipe:chicken-pesto-sun-dried-tomato-hi.pt: 2 Fatias de Pão de Fermentação Natural

recipe:squash-and-halloumi-curry-caramel.en: Squash and Halloumi Curry with Caramelised Limes

Peel the squash and chop it into 2cm chunks. Heat the vegetable oil in a large sauté pan set over a medium heat. Add the tikka masala paste and cook for 3 mins until darkened, fragrant and the oil has started to separate.
Add the squash, chopped tomatoes, water and a good pinch of salt. Cover with a lid and simmer for 20 mins until the squash is soft.

Meanwhile, finely slice the limes into wheels. Heat another drizzle of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the lime slices for about 4 mins on each side until golden and caramelised. Set aside to cool slightly.
Dice the halloumi into 2cm chunks. Heat a drizzle of vegetable oil in a large frying pan and fry the halloumi for a few mins on each side until golden all over.
Once the squash is soft, stir in the halloumi and simmer for 2 mins. Pour in 150ml of the double cream and season to taste with salt. Finely chop the cooled caramelised limes.
Spoon the curry over cooked rice. Drizzle over the remaining cream, and a dollop of mango chutney. Finish with the chopped caramelised limes, and fresh coriander, if using.

recipe:sticky-sesame-chicken-meatballs:s.en: Crush all the garlic and thinly slice all the spring onions. Combine all the ingredients for the meatballs in a large bowl, then shape into 12 equal-sized balls using wet hands.
Heat the air fryer or oven to 180°C. Cook the meatballs for 16 mins (air fryer) or 20 mins (oven) until cooked through.
Meanwhile, whisk all of the ingredients for the sauce together with 2 tbsp water in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer and cook for around 4 mins until sticky.
Toss the cooked meatballs into the sauce and stir to coat.

recipe:veggie-sheet-pan-breakfast-burrit.en: Heat the oven to 200°C. Drain and rinse the kidney beans and finely dice the pepper and onion. Transfer to a baking tray and toss with olive oil, cumin, salt and pepper. Thinly slice the mushrooms then add to a separate baking tray and toss with olive oil, salt and pepper.

Slide the kidney bean mix into the middle shelf of the oven, and the mushrooms into the lower shelf of the oven. Leave to roast for 20 mins then swap the trays and roast for another 15 mins. Once cooked, transfer both to a mixing bowl. Finely chop the fresh coriander then add to the bean and veggie mix, seasoning with salt and pepper. Reduce the oven to 160°C.

Fill a bowl with boiling water then add the spinach and leave for 30 seconds to a minute, stirring occasionally, until wilted. Drain the water, squeeze out all of the liquid from the spinach and roughly chop.
Meanwhile, add the cottage cheese to a blender and blitz smooth. Whisk the eggs into a mixing bowl then fold in the smooth cottage cheese. Season well with salt and pepper.

Line a baking tray with parchment paper, then pour in the egg mixture and dot with the wilted spinach. Slide into the oven to bake for 15 mins until golden and puffy, then flip the tray around and cook for another 5 mins. Remove from the oven and leave to cool until easy to handle if serving immediately, or until cooled completely if making in advance.
Grate the Cheddar cheese. Cut the egg into 9 rectangles. Warm the tortillas in a pan.

To assemble, start by placing the egg in the middle of the tortilla, then top with some grated cheese, a big spoonful of beans and a handful of mushrooms. Fold in the edges of the wrap to cover the filling, then roll the longest side up until sealed. Repeat until all the ingredients are used up.
Heat a frying pan over medium heat and add the wraps, seal side down – this will make sure they don’t open up. Repeat until all the burritos are sealed.

Serve immediately. Or, if making in advance, wrap each burrito in tin foil and store in the freezer. To reheat, remove the foil then dampen a piece of kitchen paper and wrap it around the burrito. Pop it in the microwave for 10-15 mins then transfer to the air fryer and cook for 10-15 mins on 180°C until piping hot throughout. These will keep for up to 3 months in the freezer and 3 days in the fridge.

recipe:spicy-pork-sesame-noodles:step:0.en: Make the tahini miso sauce: In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together all the ingredients (except the water) until smooth and creamy. Slowly add the water, a little at a time, whisking well after each addition until you’ve got a velvety sauce. Set aside.

recipe:spicy-pork-sesame-noodles:step:1.en: For the herb salad: Slice the cucumber in half lengthwise, then thinly cut into half moons. Pick the leaves from the coriander and mint, and finely slice the green tops of the spring onions (reserve the white parts for the pork). Toss everything together in a bowl. For an extra crunch and to help the salad last longer, pop it in some iced water while you finish cooking.

recipe:spicy-pork-sesame-noodles:step:2.en: For the spicy pork, combine all the ingredients for the pork – excluding the mince and oil, and including the spring onion whites – in a blender and blitz until smooth and fragrant.

recipe:spicy-pork-sesame-noodles:step:3.en: Heat a large frying pan over high heat. Once it’s sizzling hot, add a glug of vegetable oil and ½ the pork mince. Press the mince into the pan and let it brown on one side. After a few mins, use a spatula to break it up. Once fully cooked, remove the pork and repeat with the remaining mince.

recipe:spicy-pork-sesame-noodles:step:4.en: Add all the cooked pork back into the pan, then pour in the blended sauce. Stir well and cook for another 2-3 mins, making sure everything is evenly coated.

recipe:spicy-pork-sesame-noodles:step:5.en: Storage (optional): If making ahead, divide the spicy pork between 4 containers. For freshness, keep the tahini miso sauce and herb salad in separate containers. Store everything in the fridge for up to 5 days.

recipe:spicy-pork-sesame-noodles:step:6.en: When it’s time to eat, cook your noodles following packet instructions then drain and toss with the tahini miso sauce. If necessary, reheat the spicy pork in the microwave for about 2 mins until nice and hot.

recipe:spicy-pork-sesame-noodles:step:7.en: To serve, divide the noodles between plates then top with the pork and fresh herb salad. Finish with an extra drizzle of tahini miso sauce, if you like.

recipe:creamy-garlic-herb-chicken-gnocch.en: Finely dice the onion. Dice the chicken into chunks. Crush the garlic and finely chop the parsley.
Heat the air fryer to 180°C, then tip the gnocchi into the air fryer with ½ tbsp oil from the sundried tomato jar. Cook for around 15 mins until crispy.

Heat a large frying pan with another ½ tbsp sun-dried tomato oil. Add the onion with some salt, then cook for a few minutes to soften. Add the chicken and garlic and cook until softened and cooked through – about 10 minutes.⁣⁣
Add the seasoning, mixed herbs, sun-dried tomatoes and soft cheese to the pan along with 3 tbsp water. Mix it together for a few minutes.
Stir in the crispy gnocchi, the grated cheese and a small handful of parsley.
Season to taste, then share between bowls and top with more parsley and Parmesan.

recipe:creamy-garlic-herb-chicken-gnocch.pt: 50g Mistura de Cheddar e Mozzarella Ralados

recipe:miso-glazed-chicken-with-sweet-po.en: Miso-Glazed Chicken with Sweet Potato & Edamame
Peel and finely chop the garlic. Add it to a shallow bowl with the miso paste, soy sauce, honey and crunchy chilli oil. Whisk until smooth.
Score the chicken breasts in a criss-cross pattern to help the marinade sink in and speed up cooking. Add to the bowl and coat well. Transfer to a roasting tray.
Peel and cut the sweet potatoes into 3cm chunks, then toss them through the marinade.
Tip the potatoes into the roasting tray and slide into the oven. Roast for 18–20 mins, giving the sweet potato a toss halfway through.
With 5 mins to go, drizzle the broccoli with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Add the broccoli and edamame to the tray with the chicken and sweet potato.

Divide the sweet potato, edamame, broccoli and chicken between Tupperware containers. Scatter over the mint leaves and sesame seeds. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.
